item.location: appendix app:scaling 'cyclic case of the random Cayley graph argument'
item.statement: Random O(log p) frequency set lower bound is the cyclic case of Alon-Roichman
item.what_to_check: Alon-Roichman theorem statement and bib details (RSA 5(2):271-284, 1994)

chk.evidence:
The citation is at sections/appendix.tex line 196, closing the lower-bound proof in app:scaling. That proof draws L = ceil(8 ln p) frequencies at random and uses Hoeffding plus a union bound over offsets to show that the average of cos(2 pi J delta/p) is at most 1/2 for every delta != 0.

Bibliographic details:
- Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/rsa.3240050203) confirms the bib entry exactly: "Random Cayley graphs and expanders", Noga Alon and Yuval Roichman, Random Structures & Algorithms 5(2):271-284, 1994.
- Semantic Scholar (DOI:10.1002/rsa.3240050203, DBLP journals/rsa/AlonR94) agrees.

What the paper says, from the Crossref abstract: for every 0 < delta < 1 there is a c(delta) such that, for any group of order n, a random set of c(delta) log n elements gives a Cayley graph whose expected second-largest normalised adjacency eigenvalue is at most 1 - delta. The abstract adds that the result is "essentially optimal for Abelian groups".

I could not get the full text. The Wiley page returned 403 and the author-site PDFs returned 404, so I have no theorem number.

Why the attribution holds:
- For G = Z_p, the eigenvalues of Cay(Z_p, {±J_l}) are exactly (1/L) sum_l cos(2 pi J_l delta/p) for delta != 0.
- So our step is the Alon-Roichman statement on a cyclic group, with 1 - delta = 1/2 and c = 8.
- For abelian groups, the Alon-Roichman proof is the same Chernoff bound over characters plus a union bound.
- Both bounds are one-sided (on the second-largest eigenvalue), so the direction matches.

Searches: I ran no WebSearch (the session's budget was exhausted). I fetched Crossref, the Semantic Scholar API and the Wiley DOI page (403).

recommended_citations.why: Supports app:scaling line 196. A random set of c(delta) log n group elements gives second eigenvalue <= 1-delta. On Z_p the eigenvalues are the cosine averages our Hoeffding argument bounds by 1/2, so our lower bound is the cyclic instance. The abstract also says the result is essentially optimal for abelian groups.

chk.recommended_change: No correction is needed. Optionally, add doi={10.1002/rsa.3240050203} to the bib entry and sharpen the sentence to: "This is the cyclic case of the random Cayley graph theorem of \citet{alon1994random}: the averages $\frac1L\sum_\ell\cos(2\pi J_\ell\delta/p)$ are the nontrivial eigenvalues of $\mathrm{Cay}(\sZ_p,\{\pm J_\ell\})$, and $O(\log p)$ random generators push them all below $1/2$. They also note that $\Omega(\log n)$ generators are necessary for abelian groups, the expander analogue of our matching upper bound." Also cite McCracken et al. (arXiv 2505.18266, Thm 4.7/Cor 4.8) in the same place as the ML precedent for the random-log-p-frequencies margin.
